children.topic: Asymptomatic Gallstone
Underlying Pathology: Silent Cholelithiasis
Primary Diagnostic Test: Abdominal Ultrasound
Management: Observation (Conservative). Exception: Cholecystectomy if Porcelain Gallbladder or Diabetic.
Acute Cholecystitis (< 3 days)
Underlying Pathology: Persistent cystic duct block by stone
Primary Diagnostic Test: Abdominal Ultrasound / HIDA
Management: Prompt Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (within 48–72h of onset).
Acute Cholecystitis (> 3 days)
Underlying Pathology: Severe subacute local inflammation
Primary Diagnostic Test: Clinical follow-up (pulse, temp, tenderness)
Management: Conservative cool down (NPO, IV fluids, IV Cephalosporins, pethidine) -> Interval cholecystectomy in 6 weeks.
Post-Op RUQ Fluid Collection
Underlying Pathology: Leakage of bile (Biloma) or bleeding
Primary Diagnostic Test: Abdominal CT or Ultrasound
Management: Percutaneous Drainage.
HIDA: Leak + Bowel Filling
Underlying Pathology: Cystic duct stump leak (slipped clip)
Primary Diagnostic Test: HIDA Scan.
Management: ERCP and sphincter of Oddi stenting.
HIDA: Leak + NO Bowel Filling
Underlying Pathology: Major duct injury (divided/transected CBD)
Primary Diagnostic Test: HIDA Scan.
Management: Surgical reconstruction with a Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy.
Opioid-Induced Episodic RUQ Pain
Underlying Pathology: Sphincter of Oddi Dysfunction (SOD)
Primary Diagnostic Test: ERCP / Sphincter Manometry
Management: ERCP Sphincterotomy.
